title: Pull the red dust cover off an Anderson SB50 battery connector and mate both grey connectors home
instruction: Pull the red dust cover off, mate the two grey battery connectors fully together, lay the joined pair on the yellow mat, then let go and move both hands clear.
context: Industrial truck and tractor operators, 765,200 US workers (O*NET 53-7051.00, https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/53-7051.00), have the task "Perform routine maintenance on vehicles or auxiliary equipment, such as cleaning, lubricating, recharging batteries, fueling, or replacing liquefied-gas tank." Recharging means plugging the battery's lead into the charger's; Anderson's SB connectors "set the standard for DC power distribution and battery connections" (its SB50 data sheet). The SB50 is genderless: two housings fit only with one turned over; the same way up, their noses meet 14.7 mm short. One hand holds the left lead while the other pulls the red cover off its nose; one connector is turned over, brought in line and pushed home against the maker's 44 N mating force to 81.3 mm, and the pair is laid on the mat.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, on a bare bench. A flat yellow rubber mat 14 x 11 x 0.4 cm (x by y) centred at x = 25.5, y = 0. Two grey Anderson SB50 housings (P/N 992, two 1307 contacts each, a red SB50-HDL-RED T-handle screwed on the '+' face) on 6 AWG leads, lying '+' face up along y at x = 25.5 with their noses towards each other: the left one's nose tip at y = 10.1, its red 134G1 dust cover pushed onto the nose up to the handle and its strap's loop round the leads behind the housing (the cover holds the nose 0.6 cm up); the right one's nose tip at y = -6.7, lying on a 2 cm grey foam block (4 x 7.3 cm, from its nose tip to 2.5 cm behind the housing, under the handle's crossbar), its leads free behind it. Each lead's two wires are clamped to the bench 35 cm along the lead from its housing, at x = 36, y = 20 (left) and y = -20 (right), both leads' slack bowing to the left (+y). Mark the housings' places with tape.
scoring: Read at the end of the trial; nothing can fall off (both leads are clamped and the cover is tied to its lead), so no event zeroes a trial. 1.0: the two housings mated home: one turned over (180 +- 20 degrees about the axis against the other), in line (axes within 4 mm and 10 degrees), rear face to rear face 79.3 to 83.5 mm (81.3 mm on the maker's drawing); the pair lying on the yellow mat, its midpoint 2 cm or more inside the mat's edges, each housing's lowest corner at most 18 mm over the mat and pitched 15 degrees at most (a turned-over housing stands on its 13.4 mm handle); the cover off; every part of both hands 30 mm or more from the connectors and the cover; all of them still (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for the last 1.0 s. 0.5: the cover off and the two noses in line, one housing turned over, overlapping 5 mm or more (91.0 mm rear face to rear face or less). 0.25: the cover off the left nose (no part of it within 5 mm of the nose). 0 otherwise. On the bench: the 79.3 to 83.5 mm and the 91.0 mm with a caliper across the rear faces, the turn by the '+' marks (one up, one down), the 18 mm and 15 degrees with a ruler and a phone inclinometer, the hands and the last second from the video.
reset_notes: About 1 minute: pull the pair apart by the handles (44 N), lay both connectors '+' face up on their tape marks (the right one on its block), push the cover onto the left nose up to the handle, check the strap's loop is on the leads behind the housing and the leads lie as at the start.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX bodies at the maker's sizes: housings 48.0 x 36.5 x 15.9 mm, handles, the cover 46.5 x 27.9 mm; the 14.7 mm nose is a lower tongue between upper side walls (our simplification). Leads: limp links to bench clamps (real 6 AWG is stiffer). Cover on a 4-link lanyard, off at 10 N (estimate). Noses meet by contact; past 1.5 mm overlap the housings are joined where they stand by a 44 N slide (maker's mating force) standing in for the side walls that keep a mated pair in line. No pose set.
